sentences.text:
This application coming on for admission this day, the court passed the following:
 ORDER

This is the first application filed by the applicant under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of bail relating to FIR No.525/2022 dated (not mentioned) registered at Police Station Lordganj, District Jabalpur, for the offence under Sections 363, 366(A), 370(4), 376(2)(n),
109, 376(3), 370(4) of the Indian Penal Code and Sections 3, 4(2), 17, 11(6), 12 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012.

entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is in jail since 17.11.2022.

He submits that though the prosecutrix in her statement recorded before the trail Court has alleged against the Dinesh Jhariya@ Sameer Sen vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57913843/
1 present applicant saying that he committed rape upon her, but in her earlier statement recorded under Section 164 of the CrPC, she had narrated a different story and not made any such allegation against the applicant.

entities.text: Dinesh Jhariya@ Sameer Sen vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
He further submits that under such a circumstance when at the initial stage,
no allegation of commission of rape was levelled against the applicant, but subsequently, after developing a different story by the prosecutrix it is alleged against the applicant that he committed rape upon her, clearly indicates that the prosecutrix is not a trustworthy and made false allegation against the applicant. Therefore, he prays that under such circumstances, the applicant may be enlarged on bail.
On the other hand, learned Government Advocate has opposed the prayer of bail and submitted that merely in the statement recorded under Section 164 of CrPC, the prosecutrix did not make any allegation against the applicant, it does not make any difference for the reason that in the Court statement, the prosecutrix has narrated the actual story and alleged against the applicant.
Considering the arguments advanced by learned counsel for the parties, perusal of case diary and the applicant's custody period, I am inclined to enlarge the applicant on bail.
Therefore, without commenting anything on the merits of the case, this application is allowed.

It is directed that the applicant be released on bail upon his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.1,00,000/- with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court concerned for his appearance on the dates given by it.

I t is further directed that the applicant shall abide by the conditions enumerated in Section 437(3)
of the Code of Criminal Procedure.

(SANJAY DWIVEDI) JUDGE Devashish DEVASHISH MISHRA 2023.06.22 10:33:15 +05'30'
